note.p: James Mathews Leigh (ODNB) was a painter and writer who may have called on Godwin to talk about his plans for a drama on Cromwell (that eventually appeared in 1838). Both instances are in 1835. Leigh was himself the son of Samuel Leigh (d. 1831), a bookseller in the Strand. It is possible that the Mrs Leigh entries refer to J M Leigh's mother, Mary Ann Leigh (daughter of the bookseller James Mathews (1776-1835).

Godwin notes sees Mrs S Leigh and son in 1834, and there are other references to Mrs Leigh. Mrs S Leigh took over the bookselling business from her father (Samuel Leigh) aftr his death in 1831 (and she may have included her son James Mathews Leigh in the business). His 1836 text, The Rhenish Album; or, Scraps from the Rhine, was published by Leigh and Son, 421 the Strand). We have coded these several entries under this person name, since they all seem closely linked, even if it not entirely clear who is being referred to on every occasion! Also, there seems to be a Leigh, Jas in 1833, and we have included this entry.
